projects.name: baby-claw
projects.description:
A TypeScript/Node.js agent harness - a boilerplate for building focused "sniper agents" that outperform generalist agents by staying lean and purpose-built. Inspired by the OpenClaw teardown.

The core insight is that generalist agents accumulate context rot - starting at ~7,000 tokens of fixed overhead and ballooning to ~45,000 tokens after months of use, causing up to 40% performance degradation. A sniper agent starts at ~1,400 tokens and stays lean because it only loads what it needs.

Every agent is defined by four things: Triggers (cron, heartbeat, webhook, CLI/HTTP), Context injection (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, JSONL history, tool schemas), Tools (agentic loop - LLM calls tool, gets result, decides next step), and Outputs (how the agent communicates and writes to the world).

Monorepo structure: `api/` (Express backend), `web/` (Next.js frontend), `agents/` (agent workspaces), `docs/` (references, plans).

projects.name: Clean Slate
projects.description:
A personal project dashboard that auto-syncs from ~/Documents/. Shows every project you work on in a compact, expandable list with everything you need to orient yourself: what the project does, its tech stack, how to run it, where it's hosted, and which accounts it uses.

The dashboard reads from CLEAN-SLATE.md files placed in each project's root folder. A sync script scans ~/Documents/, parses these files along with package.json and git config, and writes the combined data to config/data.json. The Next.js app reads this at build time and renders a dense, monospace UI with dark/light mode - no fluff, just information.

A tools inventory section tracks all Claude Code agents, plugins, MCP servers, and skills installed locally, with source tagging (official/3rd-party/custom). A separate sync script scans ~/.claude/ for this data.

A My Toolbox view aggregates the per-project "Skills, Agents & Plugins" sections from each CLEAN-SLATE.md into a single, glanceable reference grouped by purpose - showing only the tools actually used across projects (not everything installed), with frequency counts, project lists, and origin tags. A manual overrides file (`toolbox-overrides.md`) pins favorites, normalizes categories, and supplies custom one-liners.

Each project can also declare a Chrome profile to use when opening it (via a `## Chrome Profile` H2 section, or a `Chrome Profile:` line inside the GitHub section). The dashboard shows this as a small chip next to the project name so you know which browser profile to switch to.

A clickable deployed-URL chip next to the project name opens the live deployment. The URL is auto-extracted from the Hosting section (or from an explicit `Live URL:` / `Deployed URL:` / `Domain:` line). Private/VPN-only and undeployed projects are correctly skipped.

A macOS launchd job runs both syncs automatically every 6 hours. When data.json changes, it auto-commits and pushes, and Vercel deploys the update. You never have to remember to sync manually.

A scheduled remote agent (Claude Code routine) runs weekly to check if CLEAN-SLATE.md files across projects have become stale relative to their git history, and flags what needs updating.

projects.name: Company Knowledge Base
projects.description:
A multi-user knowledge base with semantic search and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) over internal company documents. Users log in via Google Sign-In or email/password and are placed in a `pending` state until an admin assigns a role.

The core flow is: uploaded documents get chunked and embedded locally using `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384-dim vectors), then stored in Qdrant for vector search. When a user asks a question, the app retrieves the most relevant chunks from Qdrant, passes them to an LLM via OpenRouter, and streams the answer back. All conversations are persisted in PostgreSQL.

Documents are organized into Collections (e.g. HR, Engineering). Each collection maps to a dedicated Qdrant collection. Role-based access controls which collections a user can search. Roles: `admin`, `editor`, `member`, `pending`.

The admin panel covers document upload, collection CRUD, user management, model selection, a KB description editor, and external connectors (Google Drive integration exists in code but needs end-to-end testing).

projects.name: git-guard
projects.description:
A small bash pre-commit hook that catches sensitive content (paths with username, real names, client emails, server IPs, AI-assistant config files like `CLAUDE.md` / `.claude/`, local-only folders like `private/` / `docs/`) before a commit ships. When something matches, the commit is blocked and on macOS an unmissable dialog opens with three buttons: Cancel, Open in editor, or Commit anyway. The dialog title and body show which repo the commit is in and which process invoked git (terminal, launchd auto-sync, AI session) so a popup that fires without an active session is interpretable.

Designed for the workflow of using AI coding assistants where a "helpful" `git add .` can sweep in machine-local config or absolute paths before you notice.

projects.name: heartbeat-hook
projects.description:
A tiny Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook that periodically re-injects the most important rules (style, security, project isolation) into the active session so the model doesn't drift halfway through a long conversation.

Built for personal use after one too many sessions where the model echoed an API key into chat or quietly started ignoring the global CLAUDE.md rules. Tiny, copyable, immediately useful.

projects.name: JSON-LD Schema Generator
projects.description:
An internal Stormfors tool that automates the creation of JSON-LD structured data and llms.txt files for any website. The pipeline works in stages: it discovers pages via a sitemap, crawls each page using the Firecrawl API, sends the content to an LLM (via OpenRouter) to generate appropriate schema markup, validates the output against schema.org rules, auto-fixes any errors, then presents the results with copy/export buttons.

Each run is associated with a client record and is stored in PostgreSQL so runs can be revisited. A Trello comment integration allows generated reports to be posted back to Trello cards. The tool also generates llms.txt files - a machine-readable index of a site's content for LLM consumption.

projects.name: Reclaim
projects.description:
Process-aware macOS disk + memory janitor. Auditable bash. Never deletes anything you appear to be actively working on (live dev server, dirty git tree, or files edited in last 24h). Every removed path is logged to an append-only JSONL audit log. Runs on a launchd schedule with a per-category tickbox approval dialog and an "Ask Claude" escape hatch.

Cleans 6 categories (each opt-in via tickbox, with size + risk note shown):
1. `.next` caches — rebuilds on next dev
2. Installer DMGs — old auto-update installers
3. Docker unused images (full prune) — volumes never touched
4. npm cache (`~/.npm/_cacache`) — rebuilds on next `npm install`
5. Claude `vm_bundles` — skipped if Claude.app is running
6. Dormant `node_modules` — per-project sub-picker, 30d+ idle only
projects.description_short: Process-aware macOS disk + memory janitor.
stack: AppleScript (for the approval dialog and Chrome tab inspection)
projects.hosting: Local macOS tool. Deployed to `~/.disk-cleanup/` by `install.sh`, CLI symlinked onto PATH.
services:
with a 3-day gate inside `cleanup.sh` so it only actually acts every ~3 days.
- **Docker** — pruned at clean time (images + build cache; never volumes). Step skipped silently if daemon is not running.
projects.notes:
- Plist label: `dev.reclaim` (NOT `com.hanna.disk-cleanup`; changed during open-source cleanup to remove personal name from public artifacts).
- Plist is templated with `__HOME__` placeholders that `install.sh` substitutes at install time, so the deployed plist has the actual user's home directory.
- **Runtime vs source split.** Repo (`~/Documents/utilities/reclaim/`) is the source of truth. `~/.disk-cleanup/` is the deployed runtime + per-machine state (`history.jsonl` audit log, `last-run` timestamp, deployed copies of `cleanup.sh` and `reclaim`). Runtime state is per-user and stays out of git; standard `/source vs /state` split (like `~/.config/*`, `~/.local/state/*`).
- **Deploy discipline.** Always edit files in the repo, then run `./install.sh` to redeploy. Do NOT `cp` scripts directly into `~/.disk-cleanup/` — that lets the runtime drift ahead of the repo and un-committed source piles up. This bit us in 2026-07: months of source lived only in `~/.disk-cleanup/` before finally being committed.
- `docs/` is gitignored. Initial cleanup notes from 2026-05-17 archived at `docs/initial-cleanup-2026-05-17.md` (local only). Scope-expansion plan at `docs/TODO-expand-scope.md` — items 1-4 shipped 2026-06-23 (v1.4), items 5-6 still open.
